newsitem.title: USA: NY precious metals end mostly higher pre-holiday.
newsitem.headline: NY precious metals end mostly higher pre-holiday.

text.p: New York precious metals futures extended this week's recovery Friday, led by commodity fund buying ahead of the US holiday weekend, traders said.
COMEX and NYMEX metals trading ended about an hour earlier than usual Friday ahead of the US President's day holiday Monday which will close New York commodity exchanges.

"There was heavy fund participation, some activity related to the expiry of March metals options today, and position squaring ahead of the holiday Monday," Refco New York metals analyst Tim Porter said.

COMEX April gold ended up $3.70 an ounce at $346.70, after a push above Wednesday's high of $348.00 tripped buy stop orders which took the contract to an eight day intraday high at $348.60. Total estimated COMEX gold volume was 45,000 lots.
In the bullion market, spot gold ended quoted $344.50/00, compared to the London Friday afternoon fix at $342.40 and the New York close Thursday around $340.75/25.
On Wednesday this week gold fixed at a new three year low at $336.90, before a large scale short covering rally by funds led the whole precious metals complex sharply higher.

Commodity funds have been running near record short positions in gold in recent months, as talk of European central bank sales, and Western-world disinvestment from hard assets in the face of soaring stockmarkets, drove gold prices lower.
The latest CFTC Commitments of Traders data, showing the positions of funds and commercials, is due later Friday.

But physical demand in the Middle East and Far East remained near record levels, and the lack of momentum in the latest leg of the year-long downtrend triggered heavy shortcovering by commodity funds this week, analysts said.
Silver remained stronger than gold though, with the spot gold/silver ratio sliding to its lowest levels since May 1995 Friday at 65.6.
COMEX March silver ended up 11.0 cents at $5.252, its highest levels since last September, after climbing to a session high at $5.275.

While gold has been languishing near three year lows, silver broke out of a year long downtrend in mid-January on talk of commodity funds acquiring up to 50 million ounces in a gold/silver ratio spread play.

Platinum prices recovered from an early dip to end higher Friday, but palladium prices ended lower, after news Friday that negotiations on Russian-Japan supply contracts were likely to be revived sometime in March.
Palladium prices saw their highest levels since May 1996 this week after concerns about Russian supply problems.
NYMEX April platinum ended up $2.40 an ounce at $372.00, while NYMEX March palladium closed down $3.25 at $136.75.
